answers.(c): Yes, it is worth installing. Monthly bill before: 40 x 2.74 + 3 x 3.69 = 109.60 + 11.07 = $120.67. Rainwater collected each month = 1260 litres = 1.26 m^3, and this is less than the 3240 litres the garden needs, so all of it replaces tap water. Tap water used becomes 43 - 1.26 = 41.74 m^3, costing 40 x 2.74 + 1.74 x 3.69 = 109.60 + 6.42 = $116.02. Monthly saving = 120.67 - 116.02 = $4.65 (1.26 x 3.69 = $4.6494). Over the 10-year lifespan (120 months) the saving is 4.6494 x 120 = $557.93, which is more than the $420 cost, a net gain of about $138 (payback after 420 / 4.6494 = 90.3 months, about 7 years 7 months, which is within the 10-year lifespan). So Mr Tan should install the tank.
